To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) bulk viscous stresses can be consistently coupled to fluctuating decay rates in a relativistic plasma; (ii) the presence of a fluctuating bulk viscous coefficient can lead to the generation of entropy fluctuations even in the absence of a fluctuating decay rate; (iii) in the presence of a decaying fluid, the evolution of curvature fluctuations is coupled with the evolution of entropy fluctuations.

the evolution of cosmological perturbations in an interacting fluid with a fluctuating decay rate and a fluctuating bulk-viscosity coefficient is qualitatively different from the case where the bulk viscosity coefficient is not fluctuating and, in particular, that the entropy perturbation is not negligible in the case of interacting fluids with fluctuating decay rates.

(i) the evolution of the curvature fluctuations in an interacting fluid with fluctuating bulk viscous stresses is qualitatively different from that in a non-interacting fluid with fluctuating decay rates; and (ii) the evolution of curvature and of entropy fluctuations is qualitatively affected by the presence of a fluctuating bulk viscocity coefficient in at least one of two interacting fluids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the cosmological perturbations in a universe containing interacting fluids endowed with fluctuating decay rates as well as fluctuating bulk viscosity.
the development of a unified framework for the treatment of cosmologically relevant perturbations in the presence of bulk viscous stresses.
the study of the cosmological evolution of the Universe when the energy-momentum tensor is made up of two interacting fluids endowed with bulk viscosity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of cosmological perturbations, the presence of a fluctuating bulk viscous stress in the relativistic fluid may be regarded as a generalization of the fluctuating decay rates.
the presence of a bulk viscous stress in a cosmological plasma may be a useful tool in order to model the decay of an inflaton field in an effective description.
, for the class of models considered in this work, the evolution of the curvature perturbations on super-Hubble scales depends on the bulk viscosity coefficients of the interacting fluids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that bulk viscosity is a crucial ingredient in cosmological models of interacting fluids.

the present work provides a general framework for cosmological perturbation analysis in the context of interacting imperfect fluids, and it is also useful for the analysis of the evolution of cosmological perturbations in a wide range of models of the early universe.
, in the context of cosmological perturbations, the presence of fluctuating bulk viscous coefficients is a source of new and qualitatively different phenomena.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the case of interacting fluids endowed with bulk viscose stresses, the standard procedure of deriving a gauge-invariant description of the curvature perturbation by means of the Bardeen potential is not applicable.

the presence of bulk viscous stresses may have a dramatic impact on the evolution of the curvature perturbations, which can become large even if the initial curvature and entropy fluctuations are small.
the presence of fluctuating bulk viscosity may be regarded as a new source of gravitational radiation.
